text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: dedicated-redwood-prod-us-west-2 p99 generation latency > 10s for 5m. Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming). Alert ID: INC-20260314-01

devon: i'm on it — pulling p95/p99 + queue metrics. @eng-runtime please standby.

leo: seeing big queue growth, warmup concurrency looks set to 1. new instances are scheduling but staying in WARMUP state.

devon: PromQL i'm watching:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="dedicated",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
sum(increase(redis_list_length{pool="dedicated-redwood-prod-us-west-2"}[1m]))
```
queue depth ~ 480/500, p95 ~ 600ms -> p99 ~ 12.4s, streaming stalls reported.

marta: customer CS: several production customers reporting stalled streams / partial outputs. Escalating to SRE for mitigation. :eyes:

leo: logs show warmup events taking ~70-90s each and only a single warmup slot:
```
2026-03-14T19:30:05Z gpu-23 warmup started model=redwood-1
2026-03-14T19:31:15Z gpu-23 warmup heartbeat
2026-03-14T19:31:40Z gpu-23 warmup completed
```
warmup_concurrency=1 + strict_warmup_check=true -> backlog.

samir: can we bypass strict warmup? or route to smaller quantized variant for bursts? /cc @eng-runtime

devon: attempting manual scale now:
`redwoodctl capacity scale --pool dedicated-redwood-prod-us-west-2 --add 3 --reason "incident: warmup backlog"`

deploy-bot: scaling request accepted, provisioning 3 instances (type: a100-40gb). ETA ~ 60s.

devon: while that spins up, temporarily disabling strict_warmup_check for pool to allow accepting requests before full warmup. patch pushed.

leo: toggled strict_warmup_check=false on pool -> new instances now serve in degraded-mode (kv-cache not primed) but reduce stall.

incident-bot: mitigation in effect. Observability:
- queue depth -> 32
- p99 -> 1.9s
- error rate stable

marta: CS notified customers of mitigation and possible partial outputs; asking for follow-up once stable. :thumbsup:

devon: manual scale completed, warmup still happening but tail latency improved.

nora: i'm taking over the remainder of the incident (handoff). Summary: dedicated pool saturated due to burst, autoscaler added capacity but warmup_concurrency and strict warmup enforcement created a warmup bottleneck -> queue growth and p99 spikes. Mitigation steps taken: manual scale + disabled strict warmup check + routed small-variant fallback. Next: confirm post-incident config changes and run a warmup concurrency audit.

devon: thanks — passing to @nora. i'm OOO in 5.

nora: ack, i'll monitor for 30m and create postmortem draft, tagging eng-runtime + customer-success. Action items:
- revert strict_warmup_check change only after verifying cache priming script completed
- add autoscaler runbook for warmup-heavy workloads
- surface warmup_concurrency metric in dashboard

eng-runtime: noted. adding runbook item and scheduling follow-up with infra. Also recommend smaller incremental increases to warmup concurrency for this model family.

nora: closing incident channel for now; if latency regresses reopen. final note: impact window ~19:30-19:48 UTC, partial customer impact reported. We'll include exact CS list in postmortem.

devon: :wave: handing off pager to @nora

nora: :ok_hand: taking it. will post PM with timeline + RCA.
